text:
raj: ran an nsys + perfetto capture on infra-02 while reproducing the kv-cache hot path. timeline shows kernels out of order and several CUPTI activity records missing. attaching pftrace, can someone take a look?

anya: which nsys version + NVIDIA driver? we saw weird CUPTI omissions with mismatched toolkit/driver combos recently.

raj: nsys v2024.1 (nsys CLI), driver 535.98, containers are rootless (podman). capture cmd i ran: 

```
nsys profile --trace=cuda,nvtx,osrt --output=kvcache_run ./run_inference.sh
```

mike: two quick things to try: 1) add `--sample=none` / explicitly enable CUPTI activities `--trace=cuda,cupti,nvtx` so CUPTI is forced, 2) see if `LD_PRELOAD` workaround helps for older drivers. e.g. 

```
NSYS_EXTRA_ARGS="--trace=cuda,cupti" nsys profile --force-overwrite --output=out ./run_inference.sh
LD_PRELOAD=/usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libcupti.so.11.0 ./run_inference.sh
```

raj: ran with cupti trace and got failures. error when CUPTI tries to open activity: 

```
[cupti]: cuptiActivityOpen returned CUPTI_ERROR_NOT_INITIALIZED (0x1)
[nsys]: WARNING: failed to capture CUPTI activities, falling back to kernel sampling
```

olga: that `NOT_INITIALIZED` usually means CUPTI couldn't attach because perf events / perf_event_open failed in the container or driver+cupti mismatch. on rootless containers we've run into seccomp blocking perf_event and that gives the same symptom. can you paste the container syslog / dmesg around the time? also try `sudo cat /proc/sys/kernel/perf_event_paranoid` on the host.

raj: perf_event_paranoid is 2 on the host. inside the container trying perf_event_open shows EPERM in strace. dmesg has a seccomp: "BPF rejected syscall perf_event_open" line.

leo: yep, rootless + default seccomp will block perf_event. two options: run the capture on a non-rootless host, or start container with `--security-opt seccomp=unconfined --cap-add SYS_ADMIN` (or `--privileged` if you don't care). alternative is to run nsys on host and attach to the container PID namespace.

anya: before changing caps: also try a driver downgrade/upgrade matrix. we had NOTEABLE behavior where 535.60 worked with nsys 2024.1 but 535.98 dropped some CUPTI activity records due to a kernel timestamp wrap bug in the driver. if you can reproduce on baremetal host (no container) it isolates container vs driver.

raj: confirmed: baremetal run (same binary) shows CUPTI records present and kernel timelines make sense. so container/seccomp is the main blocker for CUPTI attach, but the weird timestamp reorder still showed up in container traces even after enabling perf_event. attached a perfetto trace where two kernels within the same CUDA stream show earlier end_ts than previous kernel end_ts.

mike: that timestamp wrap is often a GPU-side cycle counter rollover or a driver-side monotonic timestamp issue. check `nvidia-smi --query-gpu=timestamp --format=csv` during a run? also try using `--trace=cuda --sample=cpu` to avoid relying on CUPTI timestamps for ordering.

raj: tried `--sample=cpu` and order improves but granularity is coarse and hides micro-batching hotspots. we need CUPTI-level timestamps to reason about kernel selection heuristics.

olga: as a short-term mitigation: 1) enable `nsys --force-overwrite --trace=cuda,cupti` on a host w/ permissive seccomp, 2) use perfetto's `time_origin` fudge to realign if you need to post-process. long-term: open a bug with NVIDIA with repro (pftrace + minimal kernel reproducer).

perf-bot: Deploy Bot: NOTE: kernel 6.3.0-rc had perf_event patch backported that affects perf_event behavior; infra scheduled a kernel update in staging next week. :robot_face:

leo: also file an eng-runtime ticket referencing driver+nsys versions + rootless steps. include a tiny dockerfile + repro script that runs a tight loop of 2 kernels to show timestamp inversion (helps driver team reproduce).

raj: will do. plan: re-run on staging host after kernel bump, collect nsys+perfetto traces (both container and baremetal), open an internal issue and then file an NVIDIA bug if it repros. i'll upload pftrace link to the ticket. assigning P2 for now. :thumbsup:
